title: Light-Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) NMOS (0302), DC PP&O
raw_text:
2. MOS 0303, Light-Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt)
NMOS (0302), DC PP&O

    a. Summary. LAR Officers are the commanders or their assistants in the
Light Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) Battalions or supporting establishment
designated billets. As such, LAR Officers plan, direct and assist in the
tactical employment and deployment of LAR units. To fulfill these
responsibilities they collect information requirements, evaluate
intelligence, estimate the operational situation, and formulate, coordinate
and execute appropriate plans for armored reconnaissance and surveillance,
armored security in support of maneuver, offensive and defensive actions,
fire support, raids, communications, operational logistics and maintenance.
LAR Officers is also responsible for the discipline, morale and welfare of
their units' Marines. This MOS may be assigned only as a NMOS.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

             (2) Must have normal color vision.

             (3) Must be a 0302, Infantry Officer.

             (4) Must have a WS-B(+) water survival.



                                            1-19                       Enclosure (1)
 1106                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L



            (5) Security requirement:

                (a) Must be TS/SCI security eligible.

            (b) Must have a finally adjudicated secret security clearance
based on national agency check, law enforcement and credit check (NACLC)
prior to assignment to assessment and selection (A&S).

        (6) Must attain WS-I water survival intermediate qualification prior
to completion of Light Armored Reconnaissance Leader Course (LARLC).

        (7) Must meet MOS classification standards, as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from the Basic School.

    c. Requirements. Must complete the Light Armored Reconnaissance Leader
Course (LARLC) (M10H3W2) at the School of Infantry, Camp Pendleton, CA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (e), Infantry Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Armored Assault Vehicle Officers 55-1013.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
